guard: an empty message id is never a dedup key at ingest: two distinct id-less messages are both delivered (a third still delivers after a drain), while real-id coalescing is unchanged
why: The defect is one decision expressed at one site: which key a received id contributes to the
ingest coalescing. K1 restores the defect as it was written (key on the raw id, empty included)
and reddens the live repro cell, the one whose pre-fix observation was inbox 1 with empty-b
missing. K2 is the plausible partial relapse: only the pending-inbox lookup goes back to the raw
id while the derivation keeps guarding the other reads. K3 is the opposite authoring error, not a
relapse: a fix that stopped deduping entirely would pass every empty-id cell and silently weaken
the coalescing the cross-path transition window depends on, so the same-real-id cell holds that
side and K3 proves it holds it.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite imports the agent by RELATIVE SOURCE
PATH (../src/agent.js), so the bytes mutated are the bytes graded: no dist in the path and no
build in the command. Its package-name imports are values from @cotal-ai/core, which this change
does not touch; the mutation targets only connector-core source.
NOT PROVED HERE, named rather than implied. The write-side guards (markHandled and
protectDisposition declining to record an empty id) are not independently killable: no read
consults the empty key while the derivation guard holds, so a mutation that removes either one
SURVIVES by construction. They are kept as invariant-keeping, not claimed as kills: recording an
empty id in the handled or protected sets would arm the exact collapse this fix removes against
any future read-site relapse. The recall-lane id keys (focusExcludedIds, aheadDelivered) are a
narrower same-family residual on the focus recall path, not the ingest delivery this change
owns, and are named here so the next reader inherits the boundary rather than the surprise.
